description.narrative:
Based on requests from social partners and field observations, the Turkish Social Security Institution (SSI) developed a plan to modify KIGEP incentive eligibility conditions following the introduction of pandemic curfew. According to the plan, SSI offered to reduce mandatory premium payment days from 20 to 10 and to defer the application of the SSI overdue debts criteria. The suggested plan was approved, and the ease terms were applied between April 2020 and July 2021. A comprehensive impact assessment of those actions is currently ongoing. However, monthly employment statistics for this period demonstrate that the simplicity of terms helped to stabilize the employment retention rate for KIGEP beneficiaries and financially assist work places. In response to the impact of COVID-19 on the labour market and informality, with the implication of the Turkish Social Security Institution (SSI), the geographical coverage of KIGEP was expanded from five cities to 14 cities starting in April 2020 which resulted in an increase of 10,000 beneficiaries. During the pandemic, the importance of incentives for both employers and employees grew considerably, especially in terms of employment retention. As part of institutional attempts to build a COVID-19 response program, SSI conducted its own assessment of the impacts of Covid-19 for workers by using KIGEP data. The aim of this assessment was to understand the effect of financial incentives on job creation and employment retention under pandemic conditions. The results of the assessment also feed into the design of the employment schemes of the Government. ILO supported the SSI in the implementation of the KIGEP through increasing technical capacity of the local consultants to work for the KIGEP. The trainings mainly covered principles of the ILO approach for refugees and principles of decent work. In order to facilitate the application processes the local offices were provided with the technical equipment and the new offices were established with the support of the ILO. ILO also established a team of programme assistants placed in provincial directorates of SSI for smooth implementation of the programme and monitoring mechanism of SSI is also strengthened with increase technical capacity of SSI staff. The ILO also conveyed an orientation/information session to relevant SSI staff and the consultants in the provincial offices in order to develop further capacities to ensure a better implementation. ILO Office for Turkey together with SSI have participated in Social Security Academy organized by the ITC/ILO to present the KIGEP as a best practice.
According to the study commissioned by the ILO on an independent impact assessment of KIGEP, the overall employment increase in the enterprises that received KIGEP support (21%) was over the employment increase in the sectors in which the beneficiary enterprises operated (5%). The KIGEP support contributed five times of its volume to the national income and two times of its volume to the State's social security premium revenues. In the long term, it is projected that each 1 TRY spent under KIGEP will have an approximate contribution of 45 TRY to the national income and 16 TRY to the SSI premium revenues.

description.narrative:
Employer Incentive Programme for International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (KIKA) has been a flagship initiative of ILO in Turkey. The KIKA aims to provide incentives to employers in the Turkish labour market to promote formal employment of International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (IPs). Since 2020, 31 enterprises have benefited from the KIKA for the employment of the 130 IPs. The KIKA programme is implemented in close collaboration with Social Security Institution (SSI) and KIGEP (Transition to Formality Programme) where 100 IPs formal employment is also piloted through the incentives provided to employers.
As a response to COVID-19 Pandemic, the incentives provided for promoting IPs employment has been welcomed by the employers and the workers. This has enabled more applications to be incurred. Hence, the demand to programme has peaked when the economic activities were greatly downsized. ILO provided financial contribution to promote formal employment of the IPs through provision of incentives to employers. As the International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (IPs) are likely to be less considered by the international and national funds, thanks to this programme funded by USBPRM's, the IPs also benefitted from the programme and the awareness on inclusion of IPs in refugee focussed interventions run by the Government is increased. ILOs approach has yielded positive results and has served its purpose thereby SSI considers to include IPs in the forthcoming phases of incentive programmes.
